name: Canasta
tagline: Meld with your partner, freeze the pile, and build canastas of seven.
rulesSummary: Two decks and four jokers. Partners sit across (or play two head to head). Jokers and 2s are wild; red 3s are laid out at once as bonuses.
Each turn draw from the stock (two cards head to head), or take the whole discard pile by melding its top card. Then meld and discard.
Melds are 3+ cards of one rank with at least 2 natural cards and no more than 3 wild. Seven cards make a canasta: 500 if natural, 300 if mixed.
A wild card in the pile freezes it: then you need a natural pair of the top card to take it (also until your side has melded). A black 3 on top blocks the pile.
Your side's first meld must be worth 50 (90 from 1500, 120 from 3000; 15 below zero). Only the top card of the pile counts towards it.

You need a canasta (two head to head) to go out: meld everything, or all but one card and discard it. Going out is worth 100, or 200 concealed (melding your whole hand in one turn, with a canasta of your own and nothing added to partner's melds — no minimum needed).
With partners, you may ask “May I go out?” right after drawing. The answer binds: yes means you must, no means you can't this turn.
When the stock runs out, play goes on as long as players take the discard — and you must take it if it matches your side's meld and isn't frozen. A red 3 drawn as the last card ends the play.
Red 3s score 100 each (800 for all four), but count against a side that hasn't melded. Cards left in hand count against you. First to 5000 wins.

Three players: 13 cards each, draw two and discard one. Everyone plays alone until someone takes the discard pile: they stay alone, and the other two become partners for the hand (their melds put together, red 3s kept apart). Scores are kept per player; pagat plays to 7,500.
Six players: three pairs, partners across; three packs and six jokers, 13 cards each. A side needs two canastas to go out. Red 3s: four are 400, five 1,000, all six 1,200. Pagat plays to 7,500.
